newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids mostly stable in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids mostly stable in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices ended mostly stable Thursday in light activity ahead of the Easter holiday weekend.
High-sulpur materials in the U.S. Gulf remained the focus of market discussion amid traffic restriction on the Mississippi River after a barge carrying toxic petrochemicals capsized Monday March 17.
HSFO prices climbed last week on talk of difficulites in moving supplies around the Gulf and up to the Midwest.
But offers of high-sulphur began to slip this week on emerge supplies from the Caribbean and South America.
"It's not a huge concern. We have the supply in inventory," said one Houston resid trader, when asked about the talk of supply tightness due to traffic constraint on the Mississippi.
In the Gulf, the three percent sulphur grade tightened to $14.00-14.25 a barrel from Wednesday's $14.00-14.50, although some players pegged value as low as $13.75.
USG three percent paper continued to its recent weakness, falling to $13.50-13.75 from yesterday's $13.75-13.90. One percent physical was still near $14.88.
In the New York harbor market, spot resid values finished unchanged due to a lack of activity.
NYH one percent physical held at $15.75-16.25 a barrel. One percent NYH paper for April slipped to $15.05-15.15 from Wednesday's $15.35-50.
NYH HSFO prices were flat from yesterday with 2.2 percent keeping at $14.00-25 as recent interest seemed to have faded.
NYMEX May crude futures rebounded after losing more than a dollar per barrel in recent sessions. It settled up six cents at $20.70.
Swing gas deliveries at New York City gate was steady at $2.17-2.22 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) or $13.86 a barrel equivalent.
Natgas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, remained at $1.84/mmBtu or $11.59/bbl equivalent.
Most resid players will be absent tomorrow to observe Good Friday.
